nodes.header: Nate has been heavily focused on gaming, practicing, and tournament play (May 2022–November 2022)
nodes.body: As of 2022-05-02, Nate's primary focus has been gaming. Quote: 'Gaming has been my focus - practicing a lot and even winning a few tournaments.' He's been actively practicing and entering competitions. By 2022-06-03 he had won his third tournament of 2022. By 2022-07-10 he had won his fourth tournament — an online tournament on 2022-07-08 (Friday). On 2022-08-21 he won his fifth — his first international tournament. ~2022-09-29 he won his sixth — described as 'a really big video game tournament' with significant prize money. On 2022-11-05 he won his seventh — a Valorant championship final. As of 2022-11-04 he was helping friends 'reset their high scores at the international tournament,' showing his ongoing engagement with the international circuit. Track record of 2022 wins: 1) CS:GO team win 2022-01-14, 2) Street Fighter local win ~2022-04-25, 3) Another regional ~2022-05-27, 4) Online tournament ~2022-07-08, 5) International tournament 2022-08-21, 6) 'Really big' tournament ~2022-09-29, 7) Valorant championship 2022-11-05. Nate said on 2022-07-10 he can 'make money doing what I love' and reaffirmed on 2022-08-22: 'Gaming has brought me so much success and now I'm able to make a living at something I'm passionate about - I'm loving it.' By 2022-10-06 he reported feeling 'completely content' financially after the 6th tournament prize: 'I saved some but I'm not sure what to do with it - I'm completely content already.' Through November 2022, gaming remained central to his daily life, and he was already preparing for more tournaments after the Valorant win.

nodes.header: Joanna is allergic to most reptiles and animals with fur — face gets puffy and itchy
nodes.body: Joanna stated she avoids getting pets due to allergies. In January 2022 she specified the scope and symptoms: 'I'm allergic to most reptiles and animals with fur.' Her reaction: 'My face gets all puffy and itchy when I'm around certain animals, so I've always just stayed away.' She described this as 'really bad' and 'a bit of a drag.' She has expressed openness to finding hypoallergenic alternatives — 'I'll think about it and maybe get pets of my own soon if I can find any I'm not allergic to' — though earlier she also admitted she was 'too lazy to research alternative pets for my allergies.' Allergies developed at some point in her past — she could previously hold animals without reaction. Quote (2022-10-21): 'The name helps me remember her back when I used to be able to hold and squeeze animal[s] without an allergic reaction!' She had a dog named Tilly back in Michigan; the family had to give her up after Joanna developed the allergies. ALSO ALLERGIC TO COCKROACHES: On 2022-03-18 Joanna disclosed: 'I found out recently I'm allergic to cockroaches as well, so who knows if I'll ever get a pet.' She had recently discovered the cockroach allergy as of March 2022. She framed it as another barrier: 'I wish I wasn't allergic! I would get two turtles today if I could!' Sources: conv-42_session_2 (Jan 2022 specifics), earlier conversation about not getting pets, conv-42_session_5 (Mar 2022 — cockroach allergy disclosed), conv-42_session_24 (Oct 2022 — past ability to hold animals, prior dog Tilly in Michigan).

nodes.header: Nate teaches dairy-free desserts to others — escalated from informal sharing (mid-2022) to his own cooking show (September 2022)
nodes.body: Nate's teaching of dairy-free desserts evolved over 2022. Started informally by mid-2022 — sharing recipes with his vegan diet group and Joanna. Quote (2022-08-14): 'Since we last spoke, I started teaching people how to make this. Sharing my love for dairy-free desserts has been fun and rewarding.' Escalated to a public-facing role on 2022-09-12 when he debuted his own cooking show, teaching vegan ice cream recipes. Quote (2022-09-14): 'Last Monday I got to teach people vegan ice cream recipes on my own cooking show!' He found both phases fun and rewarding, though the public show was 'nerve-wracking to put myself out there.' Coconut milk ice cream is featured prominently in his teaching.

He shared a photo of a dessert with whipped cream and chocolate sauce. He sent the recipe to Joanna on 2022-08-14. nodes.header: Nate makes coconut milk ice cream — smooth, creamy, tropical; his personal favorite and featured dish on his cooking show debut
nodes.body: Coconut milk ice cream is Nate's signature dairy-free dessert. He has made it across multiple contexts and it remains his personal favorite. He first discovered he could make it in early Feb 2022. Quote (2022-02-07): 'I just discovered that I can make coconut milk icecream and gave it a try. It was actually pretty good, so I'm proud of myself.' He shared a photo of a bowl of ice cream with a spoon and described it as 'rich and creamy - might be my new favorite snack!' Quote (2022-09-14): 'Coconut milk ice cream is at the top of my list. It's so smooth and creamy with a tropical coconut twist. Plus, it's dairy-free for people who can't have lactose or who want vegan options.' He featured it on his own cooking show debut on 2022-09-12 (the show's vegan ice cream episode). He also made vegan ice cream and shared it with his vegan diet group (2022-06-17). Confirmed defining traits: smooth, creamy, rich, tropical coconut twist, dairy-free, accessible to lactose-intolerant and vegan eaters.

nodes.header: Joanna especially loves Nate's coconut milk ice cream
nodes.body: Joanna explicitly named coconut milk ice cream as a Nate-made dairy-free dessert she enjoys. Quote (2022-08-14): 'Yum, Nate! I love it when you make coconut milk icecream, it's so good!' It also reinforces their broader pattern of sharing dairy-free dessert ideas — Nate previously recommended coconut to Joanna for her baking, and Joanna applied it to her cake frosting.

Quote (2022-04-21, recalling her first play where she forgot her lines): 'It was embarrassing, but it taught me how important it is to prepare and stay in the moment.' This belief was forged through stage failure and informs her approach to creative work.

nodes.header: Joanna is open to returning to acting someday — 'never say never'
nodes.body: Although Joanna's primary creative identity is now writing, she remains open to returning to acting if it calls. Quote (2022-04-21): 'I'm gonna keep writing, but if acting calls out I might give it a try... maybe I'll go back to acting someday. Never say never!' She is committed to writing for now but has not foreclosed the possibility of acting again.

nodes.header: Joanna says she 'really shines' in writing — it lets her express herself in a new way
nodes.body: Writing is Joanna's primary mode of self-expression and the area where she feels she excels most. Quote (2022-04-21): 'Acting was my first passion, but now I really shine in writing. It helps me express myself in a new way.' She frames writing as a fresh form of self-expression, distinct from her earlier acting identity. This was said in the context of comparing her two creative loves.

nodes.header: Nate views fantasy and sci-fi movies as a great escape that fuels his imagination
nodes.body: Nate views fantasy and sci-fi movies as a form of escapism and creative inspiration. Quote (2022-04-21): 'I love fantasy and sci-fi movies, they're a great escape and get my imagination going.' This pairs with his existing belief that gaming is his escape from life struggles — fantasy/sci-fi cinema serves a similar function, as escape and imagination fuel.

nodes.header: Nate views playing video games as a way to express his creativity and passion
nodes.body: For Nate, playing video games is a creative and passionate outlet, not just leisure. Quote (2022-04-21): 'Playing video games is a great way to express my creativity and passion.' This adds to his existing framing of gaming (escape from life struggles, primary hobby, professional path) — he also sees it as an avenue for creative self-expression.

nodes.header: Joanna told Nate she just joined a writers group — felt inspired and like she finally belonged (2022-04-21)
nodes.body: Timestamp: 2022-04-21. Joanna excitedly told Nate she had recently joined a writers group. She described the group's members as 'inspirational people who really get my writing' and said she was 'feeling so motivated and supported, it's like I finally belong somewhere!' She shared a photo of a notebook with a notepad and a piece of paper while making the announcement. Quote: 'Hey Nate! Long time no talk! I wanted to tell ya I just joined a writers group. It's unbelievable--such inspirational people who really get my writing. I'm feeling so motivated and supported, it's like I finally belong somewhere!' Nate replied: 'That's awesome! Having a supportive group around you can really make a difference.' This was Joanna's first mention of the writers group to Nate, marking the start of what would become an ongoing community in her writing life.

nodes.header: Joanna shared 'Finding Home' script details with Nate — collaborative project with writers group (2022-04-21)
nodes.body: Timestamp: 2022-04-21. When Nate asked what Joanna was working on with her writers group, she described 'Finding Home,' a script about a girl on a journey to find her true home. Quote: 'We've made some great progress. I'm working on one with my group called "Finding Home." It's a script about a girl on a journey to find her true home. I find it really rewarding and emotional.' Nate replied that 'Finding Home' sounded special and meaningful to work on. The themes (girl finding her true home/identity) closely align with her later-completed third creative work (~May 20, 2022) about loss/identity/connection — likely a working title.

nodes.body: Timestamp: 2022-04-21. After Joanna shared her first-play story and her current focus on writing, Nate suggested she follow her passion. Quote (Nate): 'Go for it! She kept the door open to acting while remaining committed to writing as her primary focus.
